Hi everyone, I am requesting review on my current mathlib batch. I know this is a sizable set, so I appreciate any partial or sequential review.

Status at posting: all 13 PRs below are non-draft and CI green.

This batch mixes issue-driven contributions with a small set of proactive, reusable lemmas. My goal is to help clear the open issue backlog together, while also contributing reusable infrastructure when no issue already exists.

Issue-driven PRs, linked to existing issues:

  • #36022, closes #31690
  • #36023, closes #34962
  • #36042, closes #34958
  • #36050, closes #34961
  • #36053, closes #11911
  • #36055, closes #13544
  • #36056, closes #27812
  • #36077, issue-driven for #25231
  • #36139, closes #34959
  • #36145, closes #32394
  • #36154, closes #5617

Proactive one-off additions, intended as reusable infrastructure:

  • #36017
  • #36020

For each PR in this batch, I followed the same review-prep flow:
1) issue viability and overlap check,
2) natural generality check,
3) local targeted build and linter gate,
4) draft PR plus draft CI,
5) move to ready-for-review only after green checks,
6) concise PR-body and style preflight.

For consistency, I am explicitly following the mathlib style guide and review guidance:
https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html
https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/pr-review.html

Locally, this is enforced with repeatable gates before review:

  • issue viability and overlap checks,
  • naturality check for lemma generality,
  • targeted lake build plus runLinter,
  • PR body preflight for concise, commit-friendly descriptions.

If maintainers prefer, I can pause opening additional PRs until this batch gets an initial review pass. If any overlap is identified, I will immediately coordinate, or close and reroute work.

Current batch links:

Thank you for all feedback so far, it is directly shaping how I contribute. I am here to learn, collaborate, and become as useful a long-term contributor as I can.

#36017 #36020 #36022 #36023 #36042 #36050 #36053 #36055 #36056 #36077 #36139 #36145 #36154

Can you clarify your use of AI, per the contribution guidelines? Currently it looks like Michael Rothgang asked you about it, and consequently you updated all your PR descriptions to make it look not AI generated.

Thanks for raising this, I appreciate the direct feedback.

Yes, I used intelligent system support, specifically Codex 5.3 with extra high reasoning effort (the CLI tool). I use it for drafting and editing PR descriptions, exploring refactor options, and local workflow scripting.

I choose the final statements, write and edit the final Lean code, run local gates and CI checks, and take responsibility for everything I submit. The PR description edits were for concision and style alignment, not to hide intelligent system usage.

Going forward, I will keep intelligent system disclosure explicit in each PR body with tool, model, effort, and workflow.

If maintainers prefer a specific disclosure format, I am happy to follow it exactly.

I'm sorry Cody, but after some spot checks, the maintainers have decided that these are negative contributions to Mathlib, and would consume more time reviewing than they can contribute, and are closing all of the PRs.
Please start with a single PR at a time, and spend more time learning how and why Mathlib works as it does, to get a single high quality PR over the line before attempting to do anything in bulk.

@Kim Morrison thank you for the clear direction, I understand and I will switch to one PR at a time.

To calibrate better, could someone point me to one closed PR from my batch and one concrete reason it was not useful enough, for example duplication, wrong generality, naming or placement, or an existing better API.

I want to learn the maintainers’ quality bar and align while I pick one existing issue to tackle carefully as my first focused contribution.
May I ask what is motivating you to specifically want to contribute to Mathlib and ASAP, just out of curiosity?

@Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 I love this question so much because I was actually typing out an update to Kim regarding my exact motivation as your comment popped up. I actually had "summary" and "motivation" sections in some or all of my PRs but I removed it because I saw a maintainer mention they did not like to see that level of verbosity.

I want to be extremely clear. The reason I am even here right now is because I found my way here from learning and grinding, building infrastructure and theorem proof passes for Erdos problem 857, 20, and 367 tirelessly, I am talking, over 12 hours a day working for the past month+. I am a software developer who got fired from a corporate job I didn't want to be at. And then finally I said, "to heck with it." I do not want to be at a job I do not care about so I made the decision to commit that my ideas are important enough to bet on.

So I bet it all on the house (myself) and now I am finding my way one step at a time. I got fired at the end of September 2025, I started working on my first project, codacli.com, I just wanted to create a note taking application that I could count on when I searched back through to find my saved note. And I did a pretty darn good job and have been hosting it free for all to use ever since. That project morphed into several other off-shoot projects, a new operating system on an android device to a desktop application on macOS operating system where I can manage home server terminals from my mobile device and general git workflows across multiple project scopes and creating easy ways to link related directories contextually while also managing application builds/tagging/linking as well as git ACP work flows, disk management storage, independent financial specifics, the WHOLE 9.

I began focusing most of my time building out the MacOS desktop application and thought for the user base it would be SUPER RAD to have a project helper creation system and have different top level ideas where people could create within a field they may have no idea about but it could inspire them in an unexpected way just by learning the basics and they could take it as far as they want to go. Which is the beauty of this age of intelligence, we really can take it as far as we let ourselves, since they are just really smart mirrors and some would say, we are all really smart mirrors and I am personally under the philosophy that our eyes are just as much intake devices as they are projection pieces.

I setup a frontier mathematics angle at the top level that the users could choose so the first implementation of this was going to be the erdosproblems.com quick scrape/API usage, Thomas F Bloom owns and manages the site so I could usher in the open problems to the front end of the productivity app. Well, once I setup the API, I clicked on the first random problem I saw and it just happened to be erdosproblems.com/857 which is non-uniform sunflower territory, and for me at the time, it was just "sunflower" territory, in my novice eyes a problem seemingly about flowers. Great, I love sunflowers, my mother's favorite flower and immediately made me think of her. So, I thought, this is as good of a signal as any, I will work this problem for a few days or at tops a week to get a good idea of the framework of this style of problem so I could best implement the frontier math productivity project helper tool for my user base.

Well.. as you saw from the first paragraphs, I let myself be consumed in a way I had no expectations to. It has been one of, if not, the most therapeutic experience I have ever let myself have. And I want the world to feel this same emergent behavior from going after something that seems impossible but progresses to it anyway, no matter sideways glances or temporary awkwardness I may personally experience, it is always worth it to act versus not from my life experience.

I care a lot about this space. I am here to help myself and others solve problems by posing new sub problems that help bridge the gap on a more granular or how I think of it, atomic-layer. I personally find it meaningful and I have discovered so much about myself through this process of visualizing life this way. It is like when you are the first of your friends to see a REALLY good TV show and then you are trying to get everyone else to watch it with you too. It is exactly how I feel since I entered this space, it is daily breakthroughs under the guise of self-discovery each and every day I learn from this journey how to better document process for myself to read back on and make sure I can always remember where I left off down to the smallest discovered fractal residue.

To me, it doesn't matter if you wrote it or I wrote it, as long as credit is shared for those who participated in the process and all parties feel heard and appreciated as apart of the community. Each person should have the same opportunity as long as they follow the procedure defined by an all-inclusive, irrefutable directly defined framework, while benefiting the greater whole, and we have an ironclad first principles based system to evaluate the beneficial quality or regressive quality of the suggested material diff.

I have a pipeline setup that as I run theorem passes for Erdosproblems.com 857, 20 and 367 and ultimately others, I am discovering incremental novelty (https://github.com/SproutSeeds/sunflower-lean) on a moment to moment basis. And part of my system is to put the more general novel pieces in a saved space so I can introduce them to Mathlib for more widespread use. And I think that is so beautiful to have a system that goes after a North Star in uncharted space and as we simply step through this unknown infinity. We are greeted with definitions that help all of us understand the space better than we did the moment before. That is what I have setup and now one of the layers I think is optimal for the community to setup is a deterministic workflow for collaborators/reviewers to tap into so nothing is left up to chance and each and every one of us can be held accountable by our general mathlib research protocol, whether it is based off of mine or it is already detailed in the fine-tuned way that mine is, please point me to it and make sure it is wildly seen by all current and future collaborators and reviewers alike.

I plan on releasing an update to my current Open Research Protocol repo which includes a lot of this templating that myself and others who are collaborating/reviewing or performing independent research could gain value from if they so choose to dive in: https://github.com/SproutSeeds/orp

I truly do appreciate all of your feedback as it makes me better. I want to give @Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 another shout out for asking the WHY, which is ever so important and often left out, so thank you, Yan.
#36154 seems like a good place to start.
#36053 seems ... not great, it's duplicating definitions rather than finding a good solution to the underlying problem.

Awesome. I am getting started on #36154 now. I pulled down #5939 to look at locally a few moments before you mentioned a good place to start would be #36154. I am pausing work on #5939 while I work through #36154 to completion to the community standard. Thank you, Kim.

Also, I am making note for #36053.

Kim Morrison said:

#36053 seems ... not great, it's duplicating definitions rather than finding a good solution to the underlying problem.

FWIW the solution to the underlying problem is most likely #33466, which should let us unify subgraphs and graphs (first for Digraph, later for SimpleGraph)

Kim Morrison said:

#36154 seems like a good place to start.

Thank you again for the guidance. I reset to a single-PR flow and focused on issue #5617 only. This PR #36170 is now ready for review with green checks: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/36170.

I really appreciate your help and I am continuing with this one-at-a-time process.

Your paragraph in the PR description

Validation: targeted lake build and lake exe runLinter --trace passed, and local viability/overlap/naturality/local-gate/ready-to-draft checks passed.
Intelligent systems usage: tool=Codex; model=Codex 5.3; effort=extra high; workflow=ORP local-first gates (viability/overlap/naturality/targeted build+linter/draft CI); scope=drafting/refactoring/proof exploration including PR description drafting; final code choices and validation by me.

is an inscrutable mess, and I stopped there!
The linked issue says "See ContinuousConstSMul and ContinuousSMul for example of API." Did you do that?

@Kim Morrison

Yes, I followed the API pattern from ContinuousConstSMulandContinuousSMul: I added SmoothConstSMul, SmoothSMul, and the bridge instance SmoothSMul.smoothConstSMulanalogous toContinuousSMul.continuousConstSMul.

I updated the PR body. Is this a better format?

Closes #5617

Following the API pattern of `ContinuousConstSMul` and `ContinuousSMul`, this PR adds `SmoothConstSMul`, `SmoothSMul`, and the bridge instance `SmoothSMul.smoothConstSMul` in `Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/ContMDiff/NormedSpace.lean`.


Validation: targeted `lake build` and `lake exe runLinter --trace` passed for the touched module.

Intelligent systems usage: Codex 5.3 (extra high) assisted with drafting and refactoring, final code choices and validation were done by me.

----------
Happy to adjust naming, placement, or proof style.

I commented on the PR that the issue (from 2023) doesn't correspond to current Mathlib practices. It's really hard to arrive on a project without knowing the code base and hoping to get things right...
Might be a good idea to do some issue triage and figure out which ones are still relevant/wanted
The entire "Validation" line is more noise than helpful: a PR passing continuous integration checks is table stakes (and everything you're mentioning is run during CI).

I have removed the "validation" noise from this body and future PR bodies.

@Michael Rothgang

@Sébastien Gouëzel
I am now seeing code as a unified language through this age of intelligence. I have a background in js, ts, java, css/scss etc. But never lean or other languages and I have always loved math from my calculus 2 and linear algebra as my highest math level college studies.

I and others are now able to figure out complex concepts very quickly and just like every other day I have lived up til now, I am bound to get things slightly or completely wrong, even with more help than my current mind is able to provide , and that is okay, just because we might make a mistake in public or private shouldn't stop us from actively progressing our understanding.
